llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed browser automation tool, but it needs Review because it exposes powerful arbitrary-code and local-write controls through a long-running localhost daemon.

dimensions.detail: The daemon binds to 127.0.0.1 rather than the public network and uses a visible non-headless browser, which reduces exposure. However, any local process that can reach the fixed port can issue commands while it is running, and screenshot/download paths are not constrained to a sandbox directory.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a simple Node package with Playwright as the only dependency and no custom install script found. The dependency is a caret range with no lockfile, so the installed version is not reproducible and the scanner-reported Playwright advisory should be reviewed before use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation warns to use the skill only in a trusted local setting and not to run unknown code, but these are instructions rather than enforced boundaries. The skill also exposes broad Bash tool allowances including node, pw-browser, and curl.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon is intentionally started in the background, persists browser/page state across commands, and writes daemon state under ~/.pw-browser until closed. It does not appear to use an existing browser profile by default, but the active automation context can still hold sensitive session state created during use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Browser automation is coherent with the stated purpose, and the skill openly documents click/fill/screenshot/navigation plus run-code and eval. The concern is that run-code executes arbitrary daemon-side Playwright/JavaScript and can perform real web actions, read page storage, submit forms, and trigger local downloads without a technical allowlist.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the local agent and understand that this skill can control a real browser, run arbitrary Playwright/JavaScript through its daemon, submit forms, access page storage from pages it opens, and write files such as screenshots or downloads. Do not expose the daemon beyond localhost, do not pass page-provided or untrusted code into run-code/eval, close it with close --all after use, and review or pin/update the Playwright dependency before installing.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The broad browser automation surface is substantially disclosed in the top-level skill text, including daemon, eval, run-code, and file-download capability, so this is not hidden tool poisoning; it remains high-impact enough for Review.
[SDI-2] expected: The run-code implementation using new Function in the daemon is confirmed and matches the documented advanced feature, but it is a raw escape hatch without enforced approval, sandboxing, or allowlisting.
[SDI-2] expected: The eval command is confirmed and documented as page-context JavaScript execution; this is expected for the advertised advanced browser automation but can expose or mutate sensitive page state.
[SDI-1] expected: The running-code reference openly documents full browser control, storage access, downloads, and form submission. The warnings reduce under-disclosure but do not provide technical containment.
[SDI-1] expected: Download-to-disk via Playwright saveAs is documented and consistent with browser automation, but the artifact does not restrict destination paths or prevent overwrites.
[SQP-2] expected: The scanner claim of no warning is only partly supported: the docs do warn about run-code/eval risks, but the implementation does not require explicit per-call confirmation or authentication.
[SQP-2] expected: Screenshot output to a caller-provided path is confirmed; screenshots are expected, but unrestricted filesystem paths are broader than a contained artifact directory.
[SC1] unexpected: The unpinned caret dependency range is confirmed in package.json and is a supply-chain hygiene issue, not a required part of the browser automation purpose.
[SC4] unexpected: The package range starts at Playwright 1.51.0 and there is no lockfile proving a patched installed version; the scanner-reported advisory should be checked before installation.
